A trail (and its ARN) whose logs the bucket policy will allow, used for the aws:SourceArn condition and the trailName placeholder
Access to the Amazon S3 console as the bucket owner, with permission to edit the bucket policy

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/lates.goal: Grant AWS Config permission to deliver configuration history and snapshots to an existing Amazon S3 bucket by adding the required bucket policy (including cross-account setups).

prerequisites.what: An existing Amazon S3 bucket to be used as the AWS Config delivery channel destination (when not letting AWS Config create one)
Access to the AWS account that owns the S3 bucket, with permission to sign in to the console and edit the bucket policy
IAM role assigned to the configuration recorder (used for delivery when not using service-linked roles; the bucket policy must grant it permissions in cross-account delivery)
IAM permission s3:ListBucket on the configuration recorder's IAM role (needed for the HeadBucket call, required explicitly for cross-account delivery)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/u.goal: Understand how to publish VPC flow log data to an existing Amazon S3 bucket (overview page that points to sub-pages for permissions, creation and viewing)

prerequisites.what: An existing Amazon S3 bucket to receive the flow log files
Bucket permissions (bucket policy) that allow the flow logs service to write log files to the bucket

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Enable Amazon S3 server access logging on a source bucket so that access logs are delivered to a destination S3 bucket

prerequisites.what: Destination (target) S3 bucket in the same AWS Region and account as the source bucket, without Object Lock default retention, Requester Pays, or server access logging enabled, and using SSE-S3 rather than SSE-KMS default encryption

Destination bucket policy granting s3:PutObject to the logging service principal (logging.s3.amazonaws.com). The console adds this automatically, but it must be added manually for programmatic enablement (API, CLI, SDK). Alternatively, with ACLs enabled, a bucket ACL grant of WRITE and READ_ACP to the S3 log delivery group

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudF.goal: Enable CloudFront standard logging (legacy) for a distribution so that access logs are delivered to an Amazon S3 bucket

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket to receive the logs, in a default-enabled (non opt-in) region
S3 ACLs enabled on the log bucket (Object Ownership not set to bucket owner enforced)
Permissions for the user's AWS account on the bucket: s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutBucketAcl, and FULL_CONTROL in the bucket ACL, so CloudFront can grant the awslogsdelivery account FULL_CONTROL
Key policy statement on the customer managed KMS key allowing CloudFront to write logs (with kms:Decrypt if S3 Bucket Key is used), required only if the bucket uses SSE-KMS

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Make an S3 bucket configured as a static website publicly readable by disabling Block Public Access settings and adding a bucket policy granting public s3:GetObject access (plus object ACLs if needed)

prerequisites.what: An existing S3 bucket configured as a static website (the bucket to be made public)
Account-level Block Public Access settings must allow public access (edited/turned off if they are on), since the most restrictive combination of account and bucket settings applies

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/lat.goal: Understand Amazon Redshift database audit logging (connection, user and user activity logs) and what must be in place to send these logs to Amazon S3 or CloudWatch. The steps to enable it are on another page.

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket (existing or new) to receive audit logs. It must use SSE-S3 encryption only and have S3 Object Lock turned off.
Bucket permissions that allow the Amazon Redshift service to call s3:GetBucketAcl and s3:PutObject on the logging bucket
The user or IAM role that turns on logging must have s3:PutObject permission on the S3 bucket
The enable_user_activity_logging database parameter set to true in the cluster parameter group. It is required for the user activity log and is false by default.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/lates.goal: Access and work with Athena query results and query output files stored in Amazon S3 (or managed query results), including viewing and downloading them via the Athena console

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 query result location (customer-owned bucket) configured for Athena, unless using managed query results
IAM permissions for the S3 GetObject action on the query result location and the Athena GetQueryResults action for users and roles
Appropriate KMS key permissions to encrypt and decrypt the query result location, if it is encrypted

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Configure Amazon S3 Inventory so that a source bucket (or prefix) publishes scheduled CSV, ORC or Parquet object lists to a destination bucket, optionally encrypted with SSE-KMS

prerequisites.what: Source S3 bucket whose objects are to be inventoried
Destination S3 bucket where the inventory lists will be stored (can be in another account)
Destination bucket policy allowing Amazon S3 (s3.amazonaws.com, or s3express.amazonaws.com for directory buckets) to write inventory files; created automatically only when using the console
AWS KMS customer managed key (not the aws/s3 managed key) if the inventory file is to be encrypted with SSE-KMS
KMS key policy statement granting Amazon S3 permission to use the customer managed key to encrypt inventory files
IAM identity-based policy granting s3express:PutInventoryConfiguration and s3express:GetInventoryConfiguration (directory buckets only)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/lates.goal: Control and grant Athena users access to Amazon S3 data locations using identity-based policies, bucket policies, or access point policies

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket (with the data to be queried) that the policies will grant access to
IAM user, group, or role to attach the identity-based policy to (the identity that queries with Athena)
S3 Access Grants configured for trusted identity propagation identities (only for Athena workgroups using IAM Identity Center authentication)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/d.goal: Grant Amazon SES the permissions it needs for email-receiving actions: delivering to S3 (via an IAM role or a bucket policy), using a KMS key, invoking a Lambda function, and publishing to an SNS topic, including cross-account topics.

prerequisites.what: IAM role for the Deliver to S3 bucket action, which receives the permission policy and trust policy
S3 bucket that SES will write received email to
SES receipt rule and rule set containing the action (S3, Lambda, or SNS); their names and region go into the policies
Customer managed AWS KMS key for encrypting received email (optional; the default aws/ses key needs no extra setup)
Amazon SNS topic for notifications from the receipt rule
AWS Lambda function that SES will invoke
Amazon SNS topic in a different AWS account, in the same Region as the receipt rule set

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Set up the IAM and bucket permissions needed for Amazon S3 live replication: permissions for the principal creating replication rules, an IAM role for S3 to assume, and, for cross-account replication, a destination bucket policy.

prerequisites.what: Source and destination S3 buckets, whose names are used in the role's permissions policy and the destination bucket policy
AWS KMS key permissions for replicating encrypted objects (needed only if replicating SSE-KMS/DSSE-KMS encrypted objects)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/la.goal: Create a SageMaker AI execution role (IAM role with AmazonSageMakerFullAccess attached) so SageMaker AI can perform operations on the reader's behalf, and then associate it with a domain, user profile, or notebook instance.

prerequisites.what: AWS CLI installed, updated and configured (only needed if creating the execution role from the AWS CLI rather than the console)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/lat.goal: Create an IAM identity-based policy and a user role (with a trust relationship to AWS Transfer Family) that gives Transfer Family users access to Amazon S3 buckets or Amazon EFS file systems

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket (or Amazon EFS file system) that the user will access as target or source of file operations, which the IAM policy refers to
Permissions to use the IAM console and create IAM policies and roles
Additional KMS permissions in the policy if the S3 bucket is encrypted with AWS KMS (KMS key)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/lat.goal: Create the IAM policies and roles that give Amazon Data Firehose permission to read from its source and deliver to its destinations (S3, S3 Tables, Iceberg and others), and that give applications access to Firehose

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 bucket used as the destination (or error-delivery bucket) that the policy refers to
Amazon S3 table bucket and tables that Firehose writes to for the S3 Tables destination
AWS Glue Data Catalog table definitions (or schema registry) for data format conversion and Iceberg/S3 Tables access
Optional AWS KMS key for encrypting delivered data
CloudWatch log group and log stream for delivery error logging
Private Amazon MSK cluster, with a resource-based policy allowing the Firehose service principal to call CreateVpcConnection (when MSK is the source)
AWS Lake Formation permissions granted to the Firehose delivery role on the tables (Lake Formation access control mode)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-mana.goal: Enable or disable Session Manager session logging (to Amazon S3 or CloudWatch Logs) for sessions on managed nodes

prerequisites.what: IAM role/instance profile permissions allowing Session Manager to write session logs to Amazon S3 and/or CloudWatch Logs
screen utility installed on Linux/macOS managed nodes so log data is not truncated

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediaconvert.goal: Create the MediaConvert service role using the IAM console

prerequisites.what: A MediaConvert IAM permissions policy created in a previous procedure, to attach to the role

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: As the bucket owner (Account A), grant cross-account bucket permissions to Account B via a bucket policy, delegate them to a user in Account B, and verify access.

Administrator user AccountAadmin in Account A with full-access user policy
Administrator user AccountBadmin in Account B with full-access user policy
AWS CLI or AWS Tools for Windows PowerShell installed, with profiles AccountAadmin and AccountBadmin configured

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Generate a presigned URL to share a private S3 object with others for time-limited download, using the S3 console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs (Python), AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio, or AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code

prerequisites.what: An existing S3 bucket containing the object to share (the object is the item being shared)
AWS credentials/permissions of a user with access to the object (presigned URL uses the credentials of the user who generates it)
AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio installed
Connection from AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio to AWS account
AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code installed
Connection from AWS Toolkit for Visual Studio Code to AWS account

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/d.goal: Configure an AWS IoT rule S3 action that writes data from an MQTT message to an Amazon S3 bucket

Permission for the service to use the customer managed AWS KMS key on the caller's behalf (only if the S3 bucket data is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/lat.goal: Give an Amazon Redshift cluster permission to access other AWS resources (such as S3, DynamoDB, EMR) for COPY, UNLOAD, and CREATE LIBRARY by using role-based access control with an IAM role

IAM permissions policy on the role granting at minimum the LIST/GET/PUT/SCAN/DESCRIBE/ListInstances permissions needed for COPY, UNLOAD, and CREATE LIBRARY (e.g. AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest.goal: Configure a repository for Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery results by encrypting them with an AWS KMS key and storing them in an S3 general purpose bucket, so they can be retained beyond 90 days

prerequisites.what: IAM permissions for the reader's identity: macie2:PutClassificationExportConfiguration, the listed S3 actions, kms:DescribeKey and kms:ListAliases, plus kms:CreateKey, kms:GetKeyPolicy and kms:PutKeyPolicy if creating a new key
Customer managed, symmetric encryption AWS KMS key, enabled in the same Region as the destination bucket (existing or newly created; ARN needed if owned by another account)
KMS key policy statement allowing Macie to use the key to encrypt results
S3 general purpose bucket to store the results, in a Region that meets the Region requirements

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/u.goal: Grant the log delivery service the S3 bucket permissions (via a bucket policy) needed to publish VPC flow logs to an Amazon S3 bucket

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/l.goal: Set up IAM permissions for Amazon Transcribe: create identity-based policies, an IAM role with trust policy, S3 bucket access, and KMS key permissions from the example policies

Amazon S3 input bucket holding the media files to transcribe
Amazon S3 output bucket where Transcribe writes results
KMS key used to encrypt the S3 bucket contents (if applicable)
Customer-managed KMS key for encrypting custom vocabularies, vocabulary filters, or custom language models (if used)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrai.goal: Modify the S3 bucket policy on the destination bucket so CloudTrail can write log files from multiple AWS accounts

prerequisites.what: Existing destination S3 bucket that already receives CloudTrail logs, with an existing bucket policy to modify
Access to the AWS Management Console using the account that owns the bucket, with permission to edit the bucket policy

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudF.goal: Use an Amazon S3 bucket, S3 Object Lambda Access Point, or S3 Access Point as a CloudFront distribution origin, including adding the permissions that let CloudFront reach them

prerequisites.what: Amazon S3 Object Lambda Access Point (with its generated alias) to use as the origin
Amazon S3 Access Point to use as the origin (or behind the Object Lambda Access Point)
Existing Amazon S3 bucket holding the content, with a DNS-compliant name
AWS Lambda function used by the Object Lambda Access Point, to which CloudFront invoke permission is added
CloudFront origin access control (required for Object Lambda and S3 Access Point origins)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/lat.goal: Create an IAM role that lets an Amazon Redshift cluster access other AWS services (such as S3, Lambda, Glue and Athena) on the user's behalf, and associate it with the cluster

prerequisites.what: Customer-managed IAM policy restricting access to the specific S3 buckets and key prefixes Redshift needs for COPY/UNLOAD (recommended instead of broad AWS-managed policies such as AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess)
An Amazon Redshift cluster to associate the role with (new or existing)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Configure live replication between S3 buckets owned by different AWS accounts, using the same-account walkthrough with cross-account changes (AWS CLI profiles, destination bucket policy).

IAM role in the source account that S3 assumes to replicate objects, with a permissions policy naming the source and destination buckets
Permissions policy for the replication IAM role specifying the source and destination buckets
Destination bucket policy allowing the source account's replication role to replicate objects into the destination bucket
KMS key policy/permissions granting the source bucket owner permission to use the KMS key (only if replicating SSE-KMS encrypted objects)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadb.goal: Enable access logs for a Classic Load Balancer so that it delivers log files to an Amazon S3 bucket

Bucket policy on the S3 bucket granting Elastic Load Balancing permission to write access logs (with the account ID of the load balancer's account in the resource path)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrai.goal: Prepare the organization management account or delegated administrator account so that an organization trail can be created in CloudTrail

prerequisites.what: AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled
AWSServiceRoleForOrganizations service-linked role in the management account (created automatically by Organizations)

Permissions for the user or role creating the trail: AWSCloudTrail_FullAccess or equivalent, plus IAM and Organizations permissions to create the service-linked role and enable trusted access, and s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration if creating a new S3 bucket in the console
Trusted access enabled for CloudTrail in Organizations (required when using the CLI or API)
Manually created S3 bucket for trail logs (required when using the CLI or API)
S3 bucket policy allowing logging for an organization trail (required when using the CLI or API)
IAM role in the management account, modified to allow CloudWatch Logs delivery for member accounts (only if sending the trail to CloudWatch Logs with an existing role)
CloudWatch Logs log group in the management account (only if sending the trail to CloudWatch Logs)
List of ARNs for member account resources, needed to log data events for specific resources

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Configure live replication from a source S3 general purpose bucket to a destination bucket in the same AWS account by adding a replication rule, using the S3 console (the page also mentions the AWS CLI and SDKs).

prerequisites.what: Source general purpose bucket that holds the objects to replicate
Destination general purpose bucket in the same account to receive replicated objects
Versioning enabled on the destination bucket; the console offers an Enable versioning button if it is off
IAM role, with a permissions policy, that Amazon S3 can assume to replicate objects. The console can create it via the Create new role option.
iam:PassRole permission for the user adding the replication rule, so the replication role can be passed to S3
AWS KMS key permissions for the replication role, needed only when replicating encrypted objects
Destination KMS key (single-Region or multi-Region) for encrypting replicated objects, needed only when replicating SSE-KMS objects
s3:GetObjectRetention and s3:GetObjectLegalHold permissions on the source bucket for the replication role, needed only when using Object Lock

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Configure S3 replication so that objects encrypted with SSE-S3, SSE-KMS or DSSE-KMS (and SSE-C) are replicated, by adding KMS and opt-in elements to the replication configuration and granting the replication IAM role the extra permissions it needs

IAM role named in the replication configuration, with its permissions policy updated to allow s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication, kms:Decrypt on the source key, kms:Encrypt on the destination key, and kms:GenerateDataKey when replicating plaintext objects to a bucket with default KMS encryption
KMS key permissions for the role's account: if the KMS keys belong to another AWS account, the key owner must grant kms:Encrypt and kms:Decrypt to the account that owns the IAM role
Related multi-Region KMS key in each destination Region (only for Multi-Region key resolution). It must exist and be enabled.
Destination-account key policy granting kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on the destination multi-Region key (for cross-account replication with Multi-Region key resolution)
KMS key policy for the key that encrypts replicas must include kms:Decrypt for the calling principal when an S3 Bucket Key is used

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudW.goal: Find an AWS service in the catalog and follow its logging setup guide to enable log delivery to CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or Firehose

prerequisites.what: Additional permissions (V1 or V2 permission policies) that let the service deliver logs, which vary by service; without them log delivery fails

A specific AWS KMS key (its ARN) for the example that requires SSE-KMS with a particular key
Block Public Access settings turned off for the bucket, needed to grant public anonymous read access
Account-level Block Public Access settings turned off (if on) before adding a public bucket policy
A bucket configured as a static website (for the public read example)
Extra IAM permissions (s3:ListAllMyBuckets, s3:GetBucketLocation, s3:ListBucket) for the user when testing policies in the S3 console

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamo.goal: Import data from an Amazon S3 bucket into a new DynamoDB table using the DynamoDB console or AWS CLI

IAM identity-based policy for the user or role invoking the import, allowing the required S3 read actions, DynamoDB actions, and CloudWatch Logs permissions (create and manage log group and log streams)
S3 bucket policy in the source account granting the importing account access to the objects (for cross-account imports)
AWS KMS permissions to operate a DynamoDB table encrypted with a customer managed key (if a non-DynamoDB-owned encryption key is selected for the new table)

AWS CLI installed and configured (only when using the CLI)

Amazon S3 bucket containing the data file to import (created and populated with the data if it does not already exist)
Access permissions allowing the DB instance to read from the S3 bucket (IAM role and policy set up for S3 access)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/lat.goal: Attach example IAM identity-based policies to users, groups, or organization units to grant or restrict access to Amazon S3 buckets and objects

IAM user in the AWS account to receive the bucket access policy
IAM group containing users Mary and Carlos (and the users themselves) to attach the policy-variable policy to

IAM group AnyCompany and an IAM user for the partner, for the upload-only policy
AWS Organizations organizational unit (OU) whose ID is used in the aws:ResourceOrgPaths condition
AWS Organizations organization with service control policies (SCPs) available, to attach the policy at the organization root

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/la.goal: Export DB snapshot data from Amazon RDS to an Amazon S3 bucket (Parquet format)

Destination S3 bucket in the same AWS Region as the snapshot
IAM policy granting S3 access (PutObject*, GetObject*, ListBucket, DeleteObject*, GetBucketLocation) to the bucket and its objects
IAM role that RDS can assume for the export task, with the S3 policy attached (can be auto-created by the console)
Symmetric encryption AWS KMS key for server-side encryption of the export

Bucket policy allowing the export IAM role access to the bucket (only for a cross-account S3 bucket)

IAM policies in the external account allowing principals to use the cross-account KMS key (only for a cross-account KMS key)
kms:DescribeKey permission in the Lambda function policy (only if a Lambda function is used to export)

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudW.goal: Export all data from a CloudWatch Logs log group to an Amazon S3 bucket by creating an export task with the AWS CLI, for a bucket in the same account or in a different account

prerequisites.what: Existing CloudWatch Logs log group (my-log-group) whose data will be exported
Destination S3 bucket in the same Region as the log data (new dedicated bucket or an existing one)
S3 bucket policy allowing CloudWatch Logs (the Region service principal) to export to the bucket, with aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn conditions
Signed-in identity (IAM role/user) with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess and the logs permissions CreateExportTask, CancelExportTask, DescribeExportTasks, DescribeLogStreams and DescribeLogGroups

prerequisites.what: S3 bucket in account A (e.g. amzn-s3-demo-bucket) that the bucket policy grants account B access to

IAM user or group in account B to which the SQS delegation policy is attached
IAM role to which the service trust policy (EMR and Data Pipeline) is attached, with a permissions policy
